what_happened: verify-deploy.sh's --only-gate validation is hardcoded to the range 1-23 (two error messages + one numeric bound) and already rejects the existing gate 24, confirmed live: 'bash verify-deploy.sh --only-gate 24' -> ERROR out of range (must be 1-23). The new gate 25 this task adds would inherit the identical defect unless the bound is widened/derived dynamically from gate_registry_ids in the same edit.

A naive broad scan corpus (@extensions, @repo, or all of scripts/) for the new verdict-extraction-anchoring lint would false-positive far beyond the dispatch's 4 named exemptions: dozens of ordinary test-assertion lines across scripts/tests/*.sh that legitimately grep a test subject's [FAIL]/[VIOLATION] output, plus a real pre-existing naive-anchor extraction site at orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh:788 (SGR-safe in practice via a manual pre-strip, but outside this task's file_scope). Recommended fix (in report 01): scope the lint's default scan corpus narrowly to verify-deploy.sh + gate-verdict-extract-lib.sh + scripts/lint/*.sh only, which naturally excludes all of this without inventing new allowlist entries.

Planning inspection found two wiring obligations the research report did not name: core/manifest.json provides.scripts is an explicit hand-maintained list (a new script missing from it is silently never deployed, repaired by sync-manifest-scripts.sh --write over git ls-files), and the exemption set is tighter than the report assumed because gate-verdict-extract-lib.sh's executable pipeline anchors on a variable rather than a literal token, so only its comment lines match a literal-token candidate pattern. Both folded into the plan.

Concurrent sibling task declares agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/verify-deploy.sh and scripts/tests/test-verify-deploy-gate-selection.sh in its own file_scope for this same cycle, both of which this task must also touch (gate25_run plus the --only-gate bound fix). Mitigated in the plan by confining the verify-deploy.sh edit to a single phase and routing the new --only-gate bound assertions into test-gate-registry-resolution.sh rather than the sibling-owned selection suite.

The research report's live-verified finding that --only-gate's bound is hardcoded at 1-23 and already rejects the existing gate 24 made the bound fix a known, pre-scoped work item rather than a surprise discovered at verification time; the report's narrow hand-picked scan corpus recommendation likewise pre-empted an open-ended allowlist.
